title: The Light Was Plain
lyrics_text:
I walked around with a pocketful of dark
every block took a piece of my heart
My knees got fluent in concrete
my lungs kept catching on the stairs
I kept on climbing, kept on falling
like nobody knew I was there

And the light wasn't a clean way out
it was a door left half ajar
but through the noise and through the doubt
it never looked that far

Still I kept moving toward it
one sore mile, then another
Still I kept moving toward it
even when the dark pulled me under

Some nights I wore panic like a jacket
some mornings I wore it as my name
But the farther I carried that heavy weight
the less I answered when it came

And the light wasn't a halo
it was a handrail, it was a hand
somebody steady, somebody slow
holding me up till I could stand

Still I kept moving toward it
one sore mile, then another
Still I kept moving toward it
even when the dark pulled me under

You can turn around now
this road keeps receipts
I've paid for every street
I'm not turning back

Still I kept moving toward it
one sore mile, then another
And when I got there
when I finally got there
nothing in me went flying
I just let my hands up, no crying
I just let my hands open

No choir came down from the sky
just the hum of the fridge and a quiet night
a room that stayed put, no one asking why
The light was plain
and I could stay here
